pr_title: EQL: Introduce list declaration for `:` operator
pr_body:
Add syntactic sugar for performing case-insensitive comparison,
including support for the wildcard pattern, against multiple values.

type where field : ("a", "b", "c*")

Fix #64388

issue_context.title: EQL: Support multiple parameters for string
issue_context.body:
- [ ] Enumeration for `:` operator

Since string comparison (whether insensitive or against a pattern) is common in EQL, the following query is quite common:

```
process where field : "value1" or field : "value2" or field : "value3"
```

This can be simplified through the following syntactic sugar:

```
process where field : ("value1", "value2", "value3")
```

A similar concept of `in` applied on the `:` operator. Do note that differently from `in`, only string literals are allowed in this format.

It's worth investigating whether the grammar can support this concept and whether there are some constraints. As a follow-up

- [ ] Extend enumeration for regular expressions

Following #64387, the same concept can be applied on the newly introduced keywords so that multiple values can be easily declared.
